column11: Opdivo (nivolumab, HCPCS J9299), CMS Part B 2025 from the quarterly companion bf6a5b3b-31ee-4abb-b1ad-2607a1e7510a, row '2025 (Q1-Q4)': $1,996,916,016.40 over 26,991 beneficiaries = $73,984.51 per beneficiary. Discount: the biosimilar-to-reference ASP ratio in the first full year after Amgen launched Mvasi and Kanjinti in July 2019, from CMS Part B spending per dosage unit in 2020 (drug_demand): Mvasi $62.43 against Avastin $70.86, and Kanjinti $81.55 against Herceptin $91.78. Converted to ASP by the Part B payment rule then in force: the reference is paid at ASP + 6%, and a biosimilar at its own ASP + 6% of the reference's ASP (Social Security Act 1847A(b)(8); CMS, 'Frequently Asked Questions: Inflation Reduction Act Biosimilars Temporary Payment Increase', cms.gov/files/document/biosimilar-faqs.pdf). Reference ASP is 66.85 and 86.59; biosimilar ASP is 62.43 - 0.06 x 66.85 = 58.42 and 81.55 - 0.06 x 86.59 = 76.35. ASP ratios are 0.8739 (Mvasi) and 0.8818 (Kanjinti), mean 0.8778. $73,984.51 x 0.8778 = $64,947
column12: Judgement on construction: Opdivo's Part B figure scaled by the net-to-net (ASP) ratio Amgen's own IV oncology biosimilars took in Medicare in their first full year, so that the house Part B deduction in gross_to_net_pct lands the net on the biosimilar's ASP, $61,271. It is not ABP 206's own Medicare allowed amount, which would carry an add-on on the reference's ASP. Check: Horn et al. (JCO Oncol Pract 2023;19(4):e476, doi:10.1200/OP.22.00639) find the first trastuzumab biosimilar priced 15% below the originator in 2019. The 2024 annual figure was $71,752 ($1,933,800,338 over 26,951, drug_demand), so 2025 is 3.1% higher; no inflation to the 2029 launch is applied. A beneficiary's spend covers about 0.37 of a year's labelled dose (see discontinuation_pct), so this is a price per patient treated in a year, not per full year on drug. Price erosion after launch is carried separately in net_price_decline_pct

column12: Judgement on which comparator. The engine reads this key (forecast._price_factor), and a biosimilar's defining economics is its price erosion after launch: Mvasi's ASP fell to 30% of Avastin's by 2024 and Kanjinti's to 17% of Herceptin's. Leaving it null would hold the launch price flat for the whole horizon, the most aggressive reading. Mvasi's rate is taken rather than the 29.9% mean of the two, because the engine compounds one constant rate across the horizon and declines slow after year four. Mvasi also held its Medicare volume (12,306 beneficiaries in 2020, 13,212 in 2024), where Kanjinti's fell from 7,550 to 3,365 against four other trastuzumab biosimilars (Horn et al.). The case for faster: Kanjinti's 36.7%, and a crowded first wave of PD-1 biosimilars. The case for slower: Kim et al. (JCO Oncol Pract 2026, doi:10.1200/OP-26-00259) put the bevacizumab biosimilar mean allowed amount at $69.70 (2019) and $33.36 (2023), 16.8% a year on the allowed basis, and Mvasi's own yearly ASP falls were 19.4%, 35.7%, 22.9% and 12.5%, slowing by 2024. The engine freezes the factor at the LOE year it assumes for an unlaunched biologic (launch plus 12, so 2041), where 23.1% compounded prices 2041 at 4.3% of 2029

column11: drug_demand Opdivo, CMS Part B 2024, the latest year that carries dosage units (the 2025 quarterly file has none): 62,964,187 dosage units over 26,951 beneficiaries = 2,336 mg per beneficiary. HCPCS J9299 is 'injection, nivolumab, 1 mg'. A full labelled year is 6,240 mg (240 mg x 26 or 480 mg x 13; Opdivo USPI), so a beneficiary averages 0.3744 of a year on drug, and 1 - 0.3744 = 0.6256. The ratio is stable across 2020 to 2024 (0.392, 0.382, 0.382, 0.378, 0.374)
column12: Judgement on method. The pool is Opdivo's own patients across every indication, so this is measured on them rather than taken from one melanoma trial's median. Under a constant hazard in a steady state, the share of a year's treated patients (beneficiaries) still on drug into the next year equals the patient-years per beneficiary, 0.374, so the engine's stock (S = S x (1-d) + new) is the count of beneficiaries the per-beneficiary price is quoted on. The implied hazard is 1.67 a year, a median time on drug of 5.0 months. eligible_pct is built from this value (new starts = treated patients x 0.6256), so changing one without the other moves the steady-state patient count. The case against: dose holds, weight-based doses and the 1 mg/kg nivolumab induction with ipilimumab lower mg per patient-year and overstate stopping; fixed one-year adjuvant use understates it

(2) The IV share of US nivolumab revenue in H1 2026: Opdivo $2,575mm against Opdivo Qvantig (subcutaneous, which a biosimilar of the IV product cannot substitute) $337mm, so 88.43% (BMS Q2 2026 10-Q 0000014272-26-000020). 87,526 x 0.8843 = 77,396. column12: The pool is Opdivo's own IV-treated patients, not a disease. A biosimilar takes the reference product's patients across every labelled indication it is extrapolated to (lung, kidney, bladder, gastro-oesophageal, liver, melanoma and others), not the melanoma population its similarity trials enrolled. Melanoma is used only because the indication must be one of the asset's own. The share is a scaling of the book's melanoma incidence to Opdivo's IV new starts, not a melanoma eligibility filter. Check: 77,396 x $69,797 = $5,402mm, the IV share of FY2025 US nivolumab revenue, so the pool reproduces the reference's revenue at its own net price. At 39% penetration the steady-state treated stock is 0.39 x 77,396 = 30,184 US patients, before the ex-US multiple. The case for higher: BMS's net revenue per patient sits below ASP because of Medicaid rebates and 340B, so the count understates patients. The case for lower: Qvantig reached 12.7% of US nivolumab revenue in Q2 2026 ($206mm against $1,417mm) and BMS will convert more before 2028. Opdualag (nivolumab with relatlimab) is a separate product and is excluded

column11: Kanjinti, Amgen's first-to-market trastuzumab biosimilar, held 39.6% of Medicare trastuzumab claims by December 2020, against Herceptin's 45.3% (Chen et al., 'Cancer Drug Trastuzumab And Its Biosimilars Compete On Price For Market Share', Health Aff 2023;42(6):779-784, doi:10.1377/hlthaff.2022.01448, Medicare fee-for-service claims 2019 to 2020, as reported by AJMC, 'Trastuzumab Biosimilars Successfully Drove Down Prices', 2023-06-05). Cross-check on Mvasi: bevacizumab biosimilars held 57.5% of Medicare Part B in 2021 (Kim et al., JCO Oncol Pract 2026, doi:10.1200/OP-26-00259, PMID 42413074). Mvasi had 15,239 of the 22,574 Part B beneficiaries on the only two bevacizumab biosimilars then marketed (Zirabev 7,335; drug_demand), 67.5%, and 0.575 x 0.675 = 38.8%
column12: Judgement: a multiple of 1.0 on Amgen's own measured first-mover share of the molecule in Medicare, from two products that agree at 39%. This is ABP 206's share, not the whole biosimilar class, which reached 61.3% of bevacizumab in Medicare Part B by 2023 (Kim et al.). It assumes ABP 206 is in the first wave, which Amgen states (Fierce Pharma, 2026-09-16). The case for lower: a first mover's share erodes as later entrants undercut. Kanjinti's Medicare beneficiaries fell from 7,550 (2021) to 3,365 (2024), and Mvasi held at most 51% of biosimilar beneficiaries by 2023 (12,502 against Zirabev's 12,056, drug_demand) as further entrants arrived. The engine holds this share flat. Patent carve-outs, BMS contracting and the move to Qvantig all push the same way. The case for higher: commercial payers can mandate biosimilars

column11: Fitted to bevacizumab biosimilar share of Medicare Part B, Kim et al. (JCO Oncol Pract 2026, doi:10.1200/OP-26-00259): 0.5% in 2019 (launch in July), 31.9% in 2020, 57.5% in 2021, 61.3% in 2023. Normalised to the 61.3% plateau, the first full year (2020) is at 0.520 and the second at 0.938 of peak. logit(0.938) - logit(0.520) = 2.717 - 0.082 = 2.64
column12: Judgement: a measured class curve for an IV oncology biosimilar in Medicare, used because the book has no modelled biosimilar. The branded-launch curves it carries (Enhertu, k 1.08) are too slow for buy-and-bill substitution. Amgen's own products peaked as fast or faster: Medicare beneficiaries went from 12,306 to 15,239 for Mvasi and 6,950 to 7,550 for Kanjinti between the first and second full years (drug_demand). The engine applies the curve to new starts only, while the observed share included switching patients already on the reference, so the modelled stock lags the observed ramp in years one and two, which understates early revenue. The case for slower: Horn et al. (doi:10.1200/OP.22.00639) show trastuzumab biosimilars at 7% of the market in their first year and 32% in their second, and litigation could stage entry

column11: Same fit: midpoint = -logit(0.520) / k = -0.082 / 2.64 = -0.03, so half of peak is reached in the first full year (2029), as the bevacizumab biosimilars did in 2020
